language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: September 2026 was a quiet US catastrophe month. El Nino suppressed the Atlantic season, the only US landfall was Tropical Storm Edouard near the Louisiana/Texas line around 1 September, and Swiss Re called the season relatively quiet in mid-September. That points to a low September cat load, unlike August, when a derecho and Hawaii flooding hit (Allstate August cats $748M across 21 events).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The monthly CR is the line PGR trades on. The June CR of 90.0 plus the NPW miss drove -9.43% on 2026-07-15. September 2025's cat ratio was also low (0.9%), so the year-over-year cat comparison is neutral.

findings.finding: The headline arithmetic is easy. July plus August GAAP EPS is already $3.28 from the 8-Ks, so the aggregator Q3 consensus of $3.65-3.98 implies September EPS of only $0.37-0.70, below every 2026 month (the lowest was June at $1.34). Q3 2025 (EPS $4.45, CR 89.5) and September 2025 (CR 100.4) both carried the $950M Florida credit. Absent a new one-off, the release headlines a Q3 EPS beat and a year-over-year CR improvement. Florida's statute 627.066(12) books the 2025 refund as a 2025 policyholder dividend, which offsets 2025 in the next three-year test, so a repeat accrual is not implied.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats do not pay on this name. Q2 2026 operating EPS beat ($4.86 against $4.59) and the stock fell 9.43% on the CR and NPW. Q3 2025's Florida charge produced -5.78%.

findings.finding: Underlying margin has worsened three months running and largely outside cats. The August CR was 89.3 against 83.1 (+6.2 points) with a cat ratio of only 1.9%. July was +1.5 points and June +3.4. The September 2025 comparable excluding the Florida credit is about 86.5, so September 2026 likely shows another underlying year-over-year deterioration of about 2-3 points.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin deterioration caused -9.43% on 2026-07-15. In August, Insurance Business reported it as the weakest CR of 2026 with no visible reversal.

findings.finding: The FY2027 guide has no path to rise on the two new orders. The $3.6m+ medical line (Aug 11) and the $7.19m clean-energy order (Sep 30) both ship mainly in FY2028 (from 1 March 2027). The Aug 20 annual-meeting deck restated FY27 as flat to modest growth and flagged US clean-energy policy headwinds. Q1 had no solar shipments and clean energy fell 90%. So the print most likely reiterates a flat year into a +56% run.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 28 2026, when the FY27 flat-to-modest guide was first given with record FY26 profit: -8.47%. Oct 14 2025, guide raised to modest growth: -3.57%.

findings.finding: Gross margin is likely to fall back from Q1's 57%. The CEO said in the Q1 release that this level is not representative of every quarter, and FY26 ran at 51% with Q3 at 50%. At about $5.5m revenue and 51-53% margin, operating income is about $0.5-0.6m and EPS about $0.03-0.04, at or below a disputed $0.04-0.05 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 8 2026, a margin beat (57%) with 10% growth: +3.69%. The margin line has paid on the upside, so a reversal is the mirror case.

findings.finding: Backlog. May 31 backlog was $7.73m; the $3.6m+ medical line booked in Q2 ships in FY28, so Aug 31 backlog is likely about $10-11m. That is below the $12.26m record of Nov 2025. Counting the Sep 30 order, current backlog is likely about $17m+, a record the release or call will probably state.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 13 2026, record backlog of $12.26m announced: -0.48%. Backlog records have not moved this stock on print days; the order PRs themselves did (+18% on Sep 30).
